decided: At the end of a command, orbit prints a commit for the session to run only when adding the changes to the next commit would actually change something: a new file, or a tracked file that differs from the last commit. When the changes cancel out, such as an edit added and then undone or a file added and then deleted, no commit is printed, and a push still owed is still printed.
alternatives: offer the commit whenever git lists any change, and let the user recover from the failed empty commit
why: A commit that fails with nothing to commit would also block the push behind it. The comparison with the last commit is made on a copy of git's own record of staged files, so orbit still writes nothing in the repository. One rare case stays a known limit: a file taken out of git's tracking while left unchanged on disk still gets a commit printed, which then fails.
